This diff changes two artifacts that four other sims drive: `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh` (the refresher now commits, `run_engine` now takes a lock before the kill, `push_evidence` grew a soft mode) and the shared rig `fleet/tests/_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs` (the `systemd-run` engine branch now creates/removes `$FLEET_HOME/stub/engine-alive` and writes `events.jsonl` through a new `STUB_ENGINE_PHASES` branch; the `git` stub's `push` case grew a second guard). Static reading says the siblings are safe — `grep` finds `FLEET_STATUS_INTERVAL` set to `1` in exactly one case outside the new section (`fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot.mjs:47`, which asserts `states(ctx)` and one `status: state=running phase=gate` line, not `commitStates`), every other `commitStates` pin (`test_sandbox_boot_edges.mjs`, `_record.mjs`, `_selfmerge.mjs`, `_merge.mjs`) runs on `green()` at interval `30` with no engine sleep so the refresher never polls, and `STUB_ENGINE_PHASES` unset reproduces the single `gate` line byte for byte. What would settle it: run `node fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_edges.mjs`, `_record.mjs`, `_selfmerge.mjs` and `_merge.mjs` on this tree.; `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh`: the soft `add` path silently retires the phase. In `push_evidence`, `EVIDENCE_PUSH_SOFT` makes a failed `git add` `return 0` after a log line, and `commit_phase_evidence` ends `return 0` unconditionally — so the refresher sets `last="$p"` for a phase that was never committed, and that phase is never retried on a later poll. This contradicts the function's own comment ("`last` is committed only once the commit was actually made, so a phase the lock cost us this poll is committed on the next one"), which is true only for a lost lock, not for a lost add. No leg pins it (the rig's `git` stub never refuses an `add`), so it costs nothing in the exam; it costs one missing wave commit on a real branch. Propagating the failure restores the retry the comment promises.; `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh`: `EVIDENCE_LOCK` is `$FLEET_HOME/.fleet-evidence-lock`, the same persistent directory that holds `ENGINE_DONE_MARKER` — so a boot that died mid-commit (box reset while the refresher held the lock) leaves the directory behind, and the next boot that re-runs the engine (`engine_already_ran` false, because the marker was never written) pays `EVIDENCE_LOCK_TRIES` × 0.1s = 30s on every poll, `commit_phase_evidence` returns 1 every time, and the phase commits the claim promises are silently absent for the whole run; `run_engine` also pays a 30s wait before its kill. Nothing holds the lock at the point the refresher is started, so clearing it once there is safe and makes the lock per-run rather than per-FLEET_HOME.; unverified: the acceptance mode is `suite` and the task's Context pins four sibling sims that share this rig — `test_sandbox_boot_edges.mjs` ~82, `test_sandbox_boot_record.mjs` ~287, `test_sandbox_boot_selfmerge.mjs` ~293 and `test_sandbox_boot_merge.mjs` ~494/~1232/~1310, plus the merge sim's `no phase_refresher runs beside the fold unit` case ~863 — as "unchanged by this task". The provided EXAM EVIDENCE covers only `node fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot.mjs`, so nothing in the record exercises those four files against the changed `fleet/sandbox-boot.sh` and `fleet/tests/_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs`. Reading them makes the risk look low — none sets `FLEET_STATUS_INTERVAL` or `STUB_ENGINE_SLEEP`, so they boot at the rig default interval of 30s against an engine stub that returns immediately and `phase_refresher` never polls, and with `STUB_ENGINE_PHASES` unset the stub's `events.jsonl` line is byte-identical to BASE — but that is my reading, not an execution. What would settle it: run `node fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_edges.mjs`, `..._record.mjs`, `..._selfmerge.mjs` and `..._merge.mjs` in this clone and confirm each exits 0.; The lock-timeout fallback in `run_engine` can do exactly what the lock exists to prevent. `evidence_lock || log "evidence: lock still held — killing the refresher anyway"` gives up after `EVIDENCE_LOCK_TRIES=300` (30s) and then kills the refresher regardless. In the sandbox a phase commit is instant, but against a real remote a soft-mode `push_evidence` can spend three `git push` attempts and two `git pull --rebase` calls — comfortably over 30s on a slow network — so the timeout branch is reachable in production. `kill "$refresher"` signals only the subshell, not the `git` child it is blocked on, so that `pull --rebase` keeps running detached in `$EVIDENCE_DIR` and can still be mid-rebase when the foreground's `publishing` `collect_evidence`/`push_evidence` pair runs in the same worktree — the two-writer collision the lock was introduced to rule out, and the one the block comment claims "never happens". The bounded wait is a defensible choice (a lost commit beats a hung run, as the comment says), but the fallback should leave the worktree usable rather than assume it is. Two cheap options inside this task's own FILES: signal the whole process group (`kill -- -"$refresher"`) on the timeout branch so the in-flight git dies with its parent, and/or clear a half-made rebase before the next foreground commit, e.g. `fleet_git -C "$EVIDENCE_DIR" rebase --abort 2>/dev/null || true` on that branch. Neither is exercised by any leg, so this is advisory rather than a gap in the exam.
